images.caption: "Balls of flour", Omagh Market Well you are really buying a variety of new potato called "Queens". (Could be either British or Dublin). Some traders advertise them as "balls of flour", but in theory that contravenes the trades description act. This vendor always boils some spuds and displays them for the public to see. I wonder if he has them later for dinner.

images.caption: "Come on Tyrone". This large banner has been erected in John Street, in support of the Tyrone GAA team, which was victorious in the final football match held at Croke Park in Dublin on Sunday 21 September, 2008. The local papers mentioned from left to right are Gaelic Life, the Strabane Chronicle, the Tyrone Herald (published on Mondays) and the Ulster Herald (published on Thursdays). The offices are located a little further along John Street, see 103203

images.filename: Merchant Hotel Chandelier by Marcus Notley.jpg
images.caption: In 2006 Marcus Notley completed the design of Ireland’s largest crystal chandelier.  It was specially commissioned by the 5 star Merchant Hotel in Belfast. This lavish chandelier is 2 stories in height. It is constructed with over 2600 pieces of crystal on a gilded gold metalwork frame, all of which is suspended from a glass dome above the hotel's Great Room restaurant.
